title: Deferred telemetry gate and client resume protocol for intermittent SDKs
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Introduce a deferred telemetry gate in SDKs used by intermittently-connected clients (mobile, IoT, edge workers) that safely buffers spans/events when the agent cannot reach the collector, and a client resume protocol to reconcile buffered telemetry on reconnect without producing duplicate root spans or breaking causal chains. The initiative targets lower tail latency impact on production collectors and improves observability fidelity for clients with flaky networks.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a configurable deferred gate with size and time-based eviction
Buffered telemetry is persisted in a compact lossless serializer and can be resumed via a well-known resume handshake
Resume protocol re-homes buffered child spans under a canonical parent while preserving original timestamps and avoiding duplicate root traces
End-to-end tests demonstrate no more than 2% additional p99 latency for healthy clients and <0.1% increased duplicate-count in the backend in canary
Rollout experiments (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) have runbooks and automatic rollback triggers if duplicate rate > 0.5% or collector CPU increases > 12%
design_notes: We chose a deferred gate (buffer-first) vs. immediate-send-with-retry because backpressure from many offline clients can cause spikes and higher tail latency in hosted collectors.
Buffer format uses a compact binary sequence of span protobufs with delta-encoded timestamps to reduce footprint on constrained devices.

Resume handshake includes a short-lived resume-token and an idempotency-set snapshot: collector returns canonical trace_root_id and a reconciliation window. Clients rewrite span.parent_id where necessary on resume to avoid orphaned spans.
Trade-offs: this adds complexity to SDKs and requires collector-side reconciliation logic. We intentionally limit buffer retention to 48 hours to bound = storage and privacy concerns.
Privacy: buffered telemetry obeys customer data retention flags and local encryption at rest (AES-GCM) when configured. KMS integration optional for enterprise/private installs.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Library API - add DeferredGate abstraction to SDKs (node, python, java); config knobs: max_size, max_age, persist_path, encryption_key_ref
Phase 2: Serializer - implement delta timestamp binary serializer + checksum, tests for corruption-resilience
Phase 3: Resume Protocol - implement HTTP resume handshake endpoint on collector with idempotency token and reconciliation response
Phase 4: Collector - reconcile service adds a reconciliation worker that accepts rehomed spans and deduplicates via (trace_id, span_id, checksum)
Phase 5: E2E tests & canary rollout with telemetry dashboards and alerting
Phase 6: SDK docs, migration guide, and changelog
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Duplicate spans during resume leading to inflated metrics. Mitigation: collector-side dedupe using checksums and short idempotency window; tests simulate resume storms.
Risk: Increased storage on devices. Mitigation: enforce configurable size/time limits and LRU eviction; optional server-side abort instruction in resume response.
Risk: Security/privacy concerns for persisted telemetry. Mitigation: optional local encryption with enterprise KMS; enforce policy that sensitive fields can be redacted before buffering.
Risk: Operational complexity on collector (reconciliation worker). Mitigation: limited throughput cap per customer and canary monitoring with circuit-breaker to drop reconcile if overloaded.
test_plan: Unit tests for serializer and gate eviction policies
Integration tests: simulate intermittent network on CI (30% packet loss schedules) and assert traces reconstitute correctly
Load canary: 10% of traffic from a selected region routed to a collector with reconciliation enabled; measure duplicate-span rate and collector CPU
Chaos test: mass reconnects after outage to verify backpressure and collector circuit-breaker behavior
rollout_plan: Feature flag in SDKs: deferred_gate opt-in default=false for first canary
Canary: enable for internal mobile app and two selected partners (10% traffic) for 2 weeks
Phased ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 70% -> 100% with health checks at each step
Auto-rollback triggers: duplicate_rate > 0.5% for 1h OR collector_cpu_delta > 12% sustained 30m
monitoring_and_dashboards: New dashboard: 'Deferred Gate Telemetry' showing buffered_count, resume_rate, duplicate_rate, reconciliation_latency
Latency dashboard: p50/p95/p99 for collectors with and without reconcile enabled
Error budget: alerts when reconciliation error rate > 0.2%
